annotations.title: His ovvne croſs.
annotations.text: This croſs, for that it was the inſtrument of our redemption, and as it were the altar of the ſupreme ſacrifice, highly ſanctified by the touching, bearing, and oblation of the ſacred body and blood of our Lord, is truly called the Holy Croſs: ◦ and hath been endued with virtue of miracles, both the whole and euery litle piece thereof. For the which cauſes, and ſpecially for the moſt need memorial of Chriſt's Paſſion, it hath been viſited in Pilgrimages, honoured by feſtiual days and otherwiſe, reſerued & reuerenced of the ancient fathers, with all deuotion: as contrarywiſe it hath been abuſed of Pagans, Apoſtatæs, and Heretics, ſeeking in vaine to deface and deſtroy it. See S. Cyril li. 6 cont. Iulian. S. Hierom ep. 17. S. Paulinus ep. 11. Ruffinus li. 1. c. 7. & 8. Euagr. hiſto. li. 4 c. 25. S. Leo ep. 72. and Ser. 8 de Paſſione. Paulus Diac. li. 18.

annotations.title: To his mother.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The maruelous reſpect that Chriſt had to his mother, vouchſauing to ſpeake to her, and to take order for her euen from the croſſe in the middes of his infinite anguiſhes and myſteries a working for mankind.

notes.text: By this you see why in Catholike Churches MARIE and Iohn stand by the Roode.

annotations.title: To the Diſciple.
annotations.text: A great honour to Iohn and charge, to haue that bleſſed iewel in keeping: and an vnſpeakable comfort, that from that day forward the one was to the other mother and ſonne. virginem virgini commendauit, ſaith S. Hierom. He commended the virgin to a virgin. ◦

annotations.title: Bloud and vvater.
annotations.text: This pearſing of Chriſts ſide, though on the ſouldiars part it was done blindly and inſolently, [1] yet by Gods ordinance it conteined great myſteries, and was prefigured by Moyſes ſtriking the rocke with his rodde: [2] as this ſtreame of bloud and water drawen miraculouſly out of his dead body, running in the Sacraments of the Church after the people of God, was ſignified by the water of the ſame rocke folowing the Iſraelites in the deſert. Out of this ſide (ſaith S. Auguſtine) [3] iſſued the Sacraments. Hence (ſaith S. Chryſoſtom) [4] the great myſteries haue their beginning. Who vvarneth vs, that vvhen we come to drinke of the holy chalice, vve ſhould ſo approche, as though vve drevv the bloud out of Chriſtes ſide. And both bloud and water apart did flow forth, to ſhew vs the fountaine of the tvvo principal Sacraments, and their ſeueral matters, Baptiſme and the Euchariſt, ſpringing to life euerlaſting in the Church. [5] The fathers alſo ſay that the Church vvho is Chriſts ſpouſe and his coadiutrice in applying the bloud and water to the benefite of the Faithful, was here formed, builded, and taken out of this holy ſide of Chriſt ſleeping on the Croſſe, as [6] Eue was of Adams ſide, when he was caſt a ſleepe in Paradiſe.

notes.text: The Sacraments issued out of Christs side, and thence haue their vertue.
The CHVRCH builded of Christs side, as Eue of Adams.
